items.title: Josh Downs caught 1-of-4 targets for 13 yards in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
Xavier Worthy was held without a catch on three targets in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: It was a rainy, wind-swept night in Buffalo, but Patrick Mahomes still managed to have a decent evening. The same was not true for his former No. 2 receiver, who “zero balled” even as also-rans like Cyrus Allen and Jalen Royals caught passes. Held to just two catches in three games since Josh Downs’ Kansas City arrival, Worthy is turning into a tough hold even in 14-team leagues. - Patrick Daugherty

items.title: Dalton Kincaid caught 2-of-2 targets for 13 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Two catches looks bad until you realize Josh Allen completed only 10 throws in a rain-marred affair. It’s still sadly unsurprising Kincaid was one of the biggest victims of a run-heavy game environment. Rather amazingly, tonight was the fifth time in 10 2026 appearances Kincaid was held to three-or-fewer targets. He’s becoming more of a fringe TE1 than locked-in option, though the return of byes for Week 13 means he will probably still crack the top 12 against the Patriots. - Patrick Daugherty

items.title: Emmett Johnson rushed 17 times for 72 yards and a touchdown in the Chiefs’ Week 12 loss to the Bills, adding four catches for 24 yards.
items.text: Johnson made his third start in place of an injured Kenneth Walker this week. While the Bills did a far better job of bottling up the rookie than either of Johnson’s previous opponents, they still couldn’t shut him down entirely. After a quiet first half, Johnson punched in a goal line touchdown on the Chiefs’ opening drive of the third quarter. Johnson still managed 96 yards from scrimmage and what will almost certainly be another RB1 weekly finish, even with the Chiefs’ offense amounting to little in a torrential downpour. items.title: James Cook rushed 32 times for 117 yards and a touchdown in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: Sportsbooks correctly cratered the total of this game throughout the week to account for gusting winds, pouring rain, and a chilly temperature. Joe Brady’s response to these miserable conditions was to feed his top back for all four quarters. Cook set a season-high in carries and scored his 10th straight rushing touchdown. Buffalo’s lead back didn’t score in Week 1 and has found the end zone in every subsequent game. Cook will be a good bet to find the end zone at least once when he takes on the downtrodden Patriots next week. Per usual, Cook will be a top-five fantasy option. - Kyle Dvorchak

items.title: DJ Moore caught 2-of-6 targets for 15 yards in the Bills’ Week 12 win over the Chiefs.
items.text: On a rain-drenched, run-heavy night in Buffalo, Josh Allen completed only 10 passes. Translation, there wasn’t a whole lot for Moore to do even as he tied for the team lead in looks. That being said, volume has not been Moore’s strong suit this season, as he’s averaging just six targets. Although that number is skewed a bit by an injury-shortened Week 2, Moore hasn’t quite had the alpha role fantasy managers had in mind. items.title: Josh Allen completed 10-of-21 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions in the Bills’ 13-10, Week 12 win over the Chiefs, adding seven carries for 43 yards.
items.text: Playing in a cold downpour in Buffalo, it was a sloppy mess of a game for Allen, who posted his worst passing line of the year by every metric. The two interceptions, however, can’t be put entirely on him. The first was a tipped pass in the red zone that fell into the hands of a Chiefs defensive back. The second was a screen to Khalil Shakir, which was bobbled directly into the hands of Chiefs corner Nohl Williams. items.title: Patrick Mahomes completed 16-of-29 passes for 174 yards in the Chiefs’ 13-10, Week 12 loss to the Bills.
items.text: Neither Mahomes nor Josh Allen was able to get much going in what was supposed to be the game of the season. With rain drenching the field and pelting players, there was simply no way for either team to consistently string together successful passes. The Chiefs also committed several special teams blunders, including but not limited to a botched snap and subsequent shank by punter Matt Araiza, a tipped punt, and yet another missed field goal by Harrison Butker. items.title: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is still confident in head coach Brian Schottenheimer.
items.text: Jones said he is not considering a head coaching change. This came just minutes after the Cowboys’ catastrophic meltdown against the Eagles on Thanksgiving. Dallas gave up 22 points in the fourth quarter and lost on a last-second field goal. Schottenheimer stripped DC Christian Parker of play-calling duties two weeks ago. The Cowboys gave up 79 points to Cam Ward and Joe Milton in senior defensive assistant Mike Pettine’s first two games calling plays on defense. items.title: Elijah Moore caught 3-of-5 targets for 57 yards in the Eagles’ Week 12 win over the Cowboys.
items.text: Elijah Moore catching passes from Joe Milton makes a lot of sense on August 19, but is a little more surprising on Thanksgiving. Still, the 26-year-old was able to put together a solid day and helped set up the game-winning field goal with a couple of catches on the final drive. It’s hard to imagine Moore is fantasy relevant in Week 13 against the Cardinals, but he and Milton did appear to be on the same page. - Christopher Crawford
